summary: rustworkx is not a transitive dependency: it is declared only in ai-parrot's optional `graphindex` extra (re-exported by `wiki`), so `uv pip install ai-parrot` never installs it and a bare `uv sync` (exact env, no extras) removes it. Yet the `wikitoolkit` console script ships in core and hard-imports rustworkx on every subcommand via graphindex/__init__ → signals. ai-parrot-tools also imports it unguarded without declaring it. Fix: promote `rustworkx>=0.15` to core `dependencies` (and declare it in ai-parrot-tools), optionally also promoting the other extra-only imports on the same chain.

constraints.statement: rustworkx requires only numpy (already core-adjacent) and ships abi3 manylinux wheels; promoting it to core adds ~2.4 MB and no new C build.

graphindex extra also holds aiosqlite, orjson, pathspec, tree-sitter*, networkx — some of which (aiosqlite, orjson) are imported on the same sqlite_reader path; promoting rustworkx alone may leave a second ImportError behind it.
Precedent: e7f1dfccf fixed a similar gap by editing the extras, not core — extras are the project's chosen lean-install boundary.

hypotheses.statement: rustworkx is extra-only (`graphindex`), while the core-shipped `wikitoolkit` script hard-imports it on every subcommand; bare install/sync therefore lacks it.
hypotheses.reasoning: Direct read of pyproject + lock + a runtime import probe reproducing the ModuleNotFoundError through the exact chain.

plausible_answers: a) core dependency (recommended — CLI ships in core, wheel is small, numpy-only)
b) guarded import + helpful error, keep extra
c) both: core dep for rustworkx, guard the rest
